key_insight: The paper isolates which parts of a coding harness actually matter for autonomous coding performance, instead of treating the whole system as a black box. By fixing the execution loop and varying planning, action space, and context management, it enables cleaner component-level comparisons across models.
problem_solved: Existing evaluations of coding agents usually measure harnesses as monolithic systems, making it hard to know which design choices improve long-horizon software-engineering performance.
method: Built a lightweight coding harness with a fixed execution loop to control for confounding factors.
Varied three harness components independently: planning, action space, and context management.
Compared these component choices across four models to study their effect on coding-agent performance.
impact: This gives AI researchers and practitioners a more actionable way to design and evaluate coding agents. It helps identify which harness components are worth optimizing for better real-world software engineering results.
visual_elements: Layered harness diagram showing fixed loop and swappable components
Side-by-side comparison chart for planning, action space, and context management
Performance heatmap across models and harness variants
Pipeline icon set for plan → act → retrieve/context → evaluate
paper_title: An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents
paper_authors: Run-Ze Fan, Zihao Zhang, Simin Ma, Yebowen Hu, Shouju Wang
